note: Fri 13 Nov 2026 07:xx SGT run, re-verified against Thu 12 Nov US cash-equity close. Two new dominant facts since yesterday's brief. (1) The Oct CPI print that triggered the hawkish repricing is now confirmed: core CPI +0.3% m/m (vs +0.2% consensus, third straight month at 0.3%), headline +0.4% (vs +0.3%) -- CME FedWatch now prices a 100% probability of a December hike (~87% 25bp / ~13% 50bp), Waller (who explicitly said in his Nov 10 London speech that a 0.3%+ core print should trigger consideration of 50bp) and Dallas Fed's Logan (voter; wants 'at least two more 25bp hikes,' open to moving faster) both reinforced the hawkish turn. 10Y yield spiked to 5.107% and DXY to ~103.17 (a fresh ~19-month high) on Thu 12 Nov; jobless claims also ticked up to 200K (vs 195K consensus, prior revised up to 191K), a mild labor softening that cuts both ways for the Fed. Separately, and a genuine narrative correction vs yesterday: China's MOFCOM confirmed on 9 Nov that it extended (not let lapse) the rare-earth/battery/graphite export-control suspension through 10 Jan 2027 -- removing the near-term scarcity catalyst that was expected to drive the rare-earth basket this week (April-2025 curbs on 7 core rare-earth elements remain separately in force). macro.regime: Hawkish Fed hike cycle colliding with an AI-capex bellwether's leadership shock
macro.narrative: The Fed's hawkish repricing is now anchored in confirmed data: October core CPI printed +0.3% m/m for a third straight month (vs +0.2% consensus) and headline CPI +0.4% (vs +0.3%), pushing CME-implied odds of a December hike to 100% (~87% for 25bp, ~13% for 50bp). Governor Waller's own stated trigger for a 50bp move -- a 0.3%+ core print -- has technically been met, and Dallas Fed's Logan (a 2026 voter) wants 'at least two more 25bp hikes' and is open to moving faster. The 10Y yield spiked to 5.107% and DXY to a ~19-month high near 103.17 on Thu 12 Nov, while jobless claims rose to 200K (vs 195K forecast), a mild labor-softening signal that cuts both ways for the policy path. Layered on top of the rates story is a fresh idiosyncratic shock to the AI-capex trade itself: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned abruptly on 12 Nov amid a scandal involving an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative, sending NVDA down roughly 4-10% intraday and dragging SMH/XLK, even as AMD and Broadcom rallied on rotation -- the market's verdict so far is a leadership shock to one bellwether, not a capitulation on the capex thesis, with Nvidia's 17 Nov earnings call now a major binary catalyst. Gold's real-yield-driven rout extended to a third straight session, cracking below $3,900 as 10Y real yields and a stronger dollar out-compete a zero-yield asset; silver and miners fell in sympathy. Crypto took both shocks at once -- BTC fell to a 12-week low near $71-72k on continued spot-ETF outflows and roughly $550B wiped off total crypto market cap since October. The one genuine de-escalation: China's MOFCOM confirmed on 9 Nov it extended (rather than let lapse) the rare-earth/battery/graphite export-control suspension through 10 Jan 2027, removing the near-term scarcity catalyst that had been expected to drive the ex-China rare-earth basket this week, even though the separate April-2025 curbs on seven core rare-earth elements remain in force. Net effect: a genuinely more fragile, two-sided regime than yesterday -- hawkish-Fed valuation pressure and an AI-bellwether governance shock on one side, still-benign aggregate credit spreads and AMD/AVGO-led rotation within the AI trade on the other.
